findings.issue: Keyboard trap and dead Ctrl+F. Line 15 carries the static directives `@onkeydown:preventDefault="true" @onkeydown:stopPropagation="true"` on the `<ul role="tree" tabindex="0">`. Because both are render-time constants they apply to EVERY keydown, not only the keys the tree consumes. Verified in the running host (port 9335): with the tree focused I dispatched Tab over CDP and `document.activeElement` stayed `UL.w-tree` — a keyboard user cannot leave the tree. The stopPropagation also prevents the event ever reaching the `window` keydown listener that `wwwroot/js` installs in `wakeelUi.bindCtrlF` (WSearch), so while the tree has focus the page-wide Ctrl+F shortcut is silently swallowed and the native find is preventDefault-ed too — Ctrl+F does nothing at all. A05's tree pane sits next to a search box bound to exactly that shortcut.
findings.fix: Remove `@onkeydown:stopPropagation="true"` entirely (the tree has no ancestor keydown handler to shield, and it is what kills the global Ctrl+F binding). Replace the unconditional `@onkeydown:preventDefault="true"` with a render-time flag the handler maintains, e.g. `@onkeydown:preventDefault="_suppressDefault"` with a `private bool _suppressDefault;` set to `true` in each handled `case` of `HandleKeyDown` and to `false` in the `default:` branch before `return`, so Tab, Ctrl+F and every other unhandled key fall through to the page.

findings.issue: Search highlighting corrupts a mixed Arabic/Latin name (AGREEMENT item 55). `NameContent` (lines 358-374) splits the name at the match and calls `Bidi.Wrap` on each of the three fragments independently. When the match falls INSIDE a Latin/numeric run, that one run becomes two separate LRI…PDI isolates, each additionally prefixed with U+200F, and under the RTL paragraph direction the two isolates are reordered against each other. Reproduced in the host: typing «Arch» into the tree search turned «وحدة الأرشيف Archive» into the DOM text `وحدة الأرشيف ‏⁦Arch⁩‏⁦ive⁩`, which renders on screen as «وحدة الأرشيف iveArch» (screenshot shots/search-partial-latin.png). Whole-token matches («Archive») are fine, so the 16 tests do not catch it — Mixed_Arabic_And_Latin_Name_Is_Bidi_Isolated only checks the no-search path.
findings.fix: Never let the highlight split a Latin/numeric token. Either (a) before splitting, snap `index` and `index + SearchTerm.Length` outward to the boundaries of the Latin/numeric run they land in (same character class as `Bidi.TokenPattern`), so each token stays inside exactly one isolate, or (b) call `Bidi.Wrap(name)` once and locate the match inside the already-wrapped string (skipping U+2066/U+2069/U+200F when mapping the offset), then split the wrapped string. Add a bUnit test asserting that a partial Latin match (search «Arch» against «وحدة الأرشيف Archive») still produces exactly one U+2066/U+2069 pair around `Archive`.

findings.issue: Caret anatomy deviates from the A05 preview. The row renders `.w-tree-caret-slot` (line 108) BEFORE `.w-tree-indent` (line 120), so every caret sits in one fixed 20px gutter at the row's start edge while only the icon and name indent. Measured in the host: every caret's right edge is 1058px regardless of depth. In design/exports/preview/light/A/A05 — الهيكلية.jpg the caret travels WITH the node — caret and icon step together one indent per level (caret x in the 2.4x crop: depth0 ≈890, depth1 ≈862/858, depth2 ≈818/822; icon x: 852 / 820 / 780), so the caret always hugs its own icon. In the built version a depth-3 row leaves a growing empty gap between the caret column and its icon, and the builder's own comparison table records the opposite reading of the preview («every caret in one column at the right edge»), so the deviation was never seen.
findings.fix:
Swap the two spans in WTree.razor: render `` first, then ``. Keep the 20px caret slot reserved on leaf rows so sibling icons still align. The row `
` stays `width:100%`, so backgrounds, hover and selection remain on one full-width grid (no staircase) while the caret+icon pair indents as in A05.

findings.issue: A row that is both selected and attention loses its selection state. `.w-tree-row--attention` (line 43) is declared after `.w-tree-row--selected` (line 37) with identical specificity, so the amber `--w-attention-bg` / `--w-warning-border` overwrite `--w-primary-soft` / `--w-primary-border`. Reproduced in the host: after selecting «وحدة الدراسات» (the attention row) the only remaining selection signal was the bold weight — no tint, no primary border (shots/light-theme-tree.png). A05's tree pane is exactly the screen where the operator picks the unit that has no head, so selecting an attention row is the normal path, not an edge case.
findings.fix: Give selection precedence over the attention tint: change line 43 to `.w-tree-row--attention:not(.w-tree-row--selected)`, and add a combined rule (e.g. `.w-tree-row--selected.w-tree-row--attention { background: var(--w-primary-soft); border-color: var(--w-warning-border); }`) so the row still reads as "needs attention" through its border and its amber state chip while the selection tint wins the background.

findings.issue: The toolbar forwards `BindGlobalShortcut` to WSearch but not `ShowShortcutHint`, which defaults to true. With `BindGlobalShortcut="false"` (the gallery's setting) the box still shows a «Ctrl+F» hint chip for a shortcut that is not bound — visible in both host screenshots.
findings.fix: Pass `ShowShortcutHint="@BindGlobalShortcut"` to the `<WSearch>` in WTreeToolbar.razor, or expose a `ShowShortcutHint` parameter defaulting to `BindGlobalShortcut`.

findings.issue: `DefaultExpandAll` is applied once in `OnInitialized` from the `Items` present at that moment. A screen that loads its hierarchy asynchronously (the real A05 case: the structure comes from storage after the first render) gets an empty `_ownExpanded` and renders fully collapsed with no way to notice.
findings.fix: Move the seeding into `OnParametersSet`, guarded by a `private bool _defaultsApplied;` that is only set once `Items` is non-empty: `if (DefaultExpandAll && !_defaultsApplied && Items.Count > 0) { foreach (var key in AllKeys(Items)) _ownExpanded.Add(key); _defaultsApplied = true; }` — placed before the `Rebuild()` call.

findings.issue: When the caller uses the `Row` render fragment instead of `RowOf`, `Build` falls back to `new WTreeRow(key)`, so `Matches` (line 351) filters on the node KEY rather than on the text the operator can see, and the `<mark>` highlight never appears. Search silently stops working on that documented API path.
findings.fix: Either add a `[Parameter] public Func<TItem, string>? SearchTextOf { get; set; }` used by `Matches` when `RowOf` is null, or document on the `Row` parameter that `RowOf` must still be supplied for search and the accessible name, and skip filtering (treat every node as a match) when neither is set instead of matching on keys.

findings.issue: `SetExpanded` discards the callback task (`_ = ExpandedChanged.InvokeAsync(keys);`), so an exception thrown by a parent's `ExpandedChanged` handler during `ExpandAll()`/`CollapseAll()` is swallowed and never reaches Blazor's error boundary — unlike `ToggleAsync`, which awaits it.
findings.fix: Make the public helpers async (`public Task ExpandAllAsync()` / `CollapseAllAsync()` returning `SetExpandedAsync(...)` which awaits `ExpandedChanged.InvokeAsync`), keeping the existing void `ExpandAll()`/`CollapseAll()` as thin wrappers only if a synchronous call site is required.

findings.issue: Spacing nuance against A05: the built indent step is 16px (`--w-tree-indent`, line 5) and the row pitch is 34px; measured against the preview crop the indent step is ≈21px and the row pitch ≈38px. The pane heights happen to match (455.6px built vs ≈452px preview) only because the built tree shows one extra row.
findings.fix: Optional — if the A05 screen is to sit exactly on the preview, raise `--w-tree-indent` to 20px and `--w-tree-row-height` to 38px, or leave both as the deliberate design-system rhythm and record the choice in the package notes (the builder recorded the row height but not the indent step).

findings.issue: The tree section promises behaviour that does not exist: the sub-title is «اسحب العنصر داخل الشجرة لتغيير تبعيته.» and every row carries a handle with `cursor: grab` and the tooltip «اسحب لتغيير موضع العنصر», but the handle is a plain `<span>` with no `draggable` attribute and no drag events — nothing can be dragged.
findings.fix: Until drag-and-drop exists, change the gallery sub-title to describe the handle as a placeholder for the move affordance (or drop the sentence), and in WTree.razor.css change `.w-tree-handle { cursor: grab }` to `cursor: default` so the pointer does not advertise a gesture the component does not implement.
